1.subtopic: What Makes a Slide Clear, Not Crowded
1.outline: Term theme: 'Slides & Stories'. Look at cluttered vs clean slide examples and agree the class rule: one idea per slide, big text, not too many words.
1.sowResources: PowerPoint, Google Slides, example slide gallery.
objectives: Compare a cluttered slide with a clean one.
State the class rule for a good slide.
Identify one idea per slide in an example deck.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Cluttered vs clean
plan.detail: Project two slides on the same topic — one crammed, one clean. Vote which is easier to read.

plan.title: Spot the idea
plan.detail: Look through an example deck and say the one idea on each slide.

plan.title: Class rule poster
plan.detail: Write the class rule together: one idea, big text, not too many words. Log out.

successCriteria: I can say which slide is easier to read and why.
I can name the one idea on an example slide.
I know the class rule for a good slide.

2.outline: Open PowerPoint or Slides, choose a title layout, and create the opening slide for a personal presentation.
objectives: Open a new presentation and choose a title layout.
Type a title and a subtitle.
Save the file with a sensible name.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Title layout tour
plan.detail: Show the different slide layouts and pick the title layout together.

plan.title: Build the title slide
plan.detail: Type a title (my presentation name) and a subtitle (my own name).

plan.title: Save it
plan.detail: Save with a sensible file name. Log out.

successCriteria: I chose a title layout.
My title slide has a title and a subtitle.
My file is saved with a sensible name.

3.outline: Add two more slides after the title slide, each with one idea and one picture from the class picture folder.
3.sowResources: PowerPoint, Google Slides, class picture folder.
objectives: Add new slides to a presentation.
Insert a picture on each slide.
Keep to one idea per slide.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Add a slide
plan.detail: Demo the 'New Slide' button and choosing a layout with a picture placeholder.

plan.title: Build two slides
plan.detail: Add two slides, each with one idea and one picture from the class folder.

plan.title: Check the rule
plan.detail: Partner checks: does each slide keep to one idea? Save and log out.

successCriteria: I added two new slides.
Each slide has one picture.
Each slide keeps to one idea.

4.outline: Learn what a transition is and add one simple, non-distracting transition between slides.
objectives: Explain what a slide transition is.
Add one transition to the presentation.
Explain why too many transitions can be distracting.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What is a transition?
plan.detail: Show a plain slide change, then a transition. Discuss: does it help the audience?

plan.title: Add one transition
plan.detail: Apply a simple transition (fade or wipe) to all slides — not a different flashy one per slide.

plan.title: Play it through
plan.detail: Play the deck from the start; check the transition doesn't distract. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I can explain what a transition is.
My deck uses one simple transition.
I can say why too many transitions is distracting.

5.subtopic: Write What I'll Say for Each Slide
5.outline: Use the speaker notes area under each slide to write a short reminder of what to say when presenting.
objectives: Find the speaker notes area for a slide.
Write a short note for each slide.
Explain why notes should not be the whole script.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Find the notes area
plan.detail: Show where speaker notes live under each slide.

plan.title: Write notes
plan.detail: Write one or two short reminder sentences per slide — not the whole thing to read out.

plan.title: Practise once
plan.detail: Practise saying the slide using only the notes as a reminder. Save and log out.

successCriteria: I found the speaker notes area.
I wrote a short note for each slide.
I can explain why notes should be short reminders, not a script.

6.subtopic: Spot What's True and What's a Trick
6.outline: Play Google's Interland 'Reality River' to practise spotting online tricks, then discuss one way to check if something is true.
6.sowResources: Google Interland (Reality River), discussion prompt cards.
objectives: Play Reality River and identify tricky content.
Name one way to check if online information is true.
Explain why it matters to check before believing or sharing.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Reality River
plan.detail: Play the Interland game individually or in pairs, discussing each decision as it comes up.

plan.title: One way to check
plan.detail: As a class, list ways to check if something is true: ask an adult, check another source, look for a trusted website.

plan.title: Plenary
plan.detail: Each pupil says one check they will use. Log out.

successCriteria: I played Reality River and made sensible choices.
I can name one way to check if something is true.
I can explain why checking matters.

7.outline: Bring the term together: finish a 3-slide 'All About Me' deck with a title slide, two content slides with pictures, a transition and speaker notes.
7.sowResources: PowerPoint, Google Slides, class picture folder.
objectives: Finish a 3-slide deck about myself.
Include a title slide, pictures and speaker notes.
Check the deck against the class rule.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Finish the deck
plan.detail: Complete all three slides: title, and two content slides with pictures and short notes.

plan.title: Self-check
plan.detail: Check against the class rule: one idea per slide, not too crowded.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save the finished deck. Log out.

successCriteria: My deck has a title slide and two content slides.
Each slide has a picture and speaker notes.
My deck follows the one-idea-per-slide rule.

8.outline: Practise presenting the finished 'All About Me' deck to a partner using the speaker notes, and give kind feedback.
objectives: Present a 3-slide deck to a partner.
Use speaker notes rather than reading the slide.
Give one kind piece of feedback.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: How to present
plan.detail: Model presenting a slide: look up, use notes as a reminder, don't just read the slide.

plan.title: Partner presentations
plan.detail: Present to a partner, then swap. Partner gives one kind, specific piece of feedback.

plan.title: Portfolio save
plan.detail: Save the finished deck to the portfolio folder. Log out.

successCriteria: I presented my deck without just reading the slides.
I gave my partner one kind, specific piece of feedback.
My deck is saved to the portfolio folder.

9.outline: Extend the 'All About Me' deck with a fourth slide — favourite things — practising everything learned this term one more time.
objectives: Add a fourth slide to the deck.
Apply a picture, transition and speaker notes to it.
Keep the deck consistent with earlier slides.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Build the fourth slide
plan.detail: Add a 'favourite things' slide with a picture, the same transition style, and short notes.

plan.title: Consistency check
plan.detail: Check the new slide matches the style of the others. Save.

plan.title: Log out
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: My deck now has four slides.
The new slide has a picture and notes.
The new slide matches the others in style.

10.outline: Rehearse the whole term's skills in pairs: build a slide, add a picture, apply a transition, write notes, present.
10.sowResources: Recap slide deck, practice task cards.
objectives: Recall the term's presentation skills in order.
Rehearse building and presenting a slide with a partner.
Identify the trickiest step.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Skill recap
plan.detail: Recap: new slide, picture, transition, notes, present — as a class chant.

plan.title: Paired rehearsal
plan.detail: Build and present one slide with a partner reading the task card, then swap.

plan.title: Tricky step check
plan.detail: Name the step you still find hardest. Log out.

successCriteria: I can list the term's slide-building steps in order.
I rehearsed building and presenting with a partner.
I know which step I need more practice on.

11.outline: Individual task: build a simple multi-slide deck with a title slide, at least one picture, a transition and speaker notes.
objectives: Build a multi-slide deck independently.
Add images and a transition.
Judge whether given online information is reliable.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start — explain the task and rubric.

plan.title: Build the deck
plan.detail: Individual practical: title slide plus two content slides with pictures and a transition.

plan.title: Reliability question
plan.detail: One-to-one: show a piece of information and ask 'is this reliable, and how do you know?'

plan.title: Save and celebrate
plan.detail: Save the deck and celebrate the term's progress. Log out.

successCriteria: I built a multi-slide deck on my own.
My deck has images and a transition.
I explained one way to check if online information is reliable.
